# Title: Fix: React Context is unavailable in Server Components
# Author: StackHeal Architect
# Date: 2026-05-28
# Canonical URL: https://stackheal.vercel.app/blog/fix-context-server-components-nextjs/

## The Symptom
```text
Error: createContext only works in Client Components. Add the "use client" directive at the top of the file to use it.
Root Cause
In the Next.js App Router (Next 13+), all components are Server Components by default. React Context (createContext, useContext) is an interactive browser API that requires constant re-renders. The server cannot handle browser state. Therefore, wrapping your root layout.tsx directly in a Provider causes a fatal compilation error.

The Cure
You must use the "Boundary Pattern." Isolate your context provider into a separate file marked with "use client", and then import that wrapper into your server-rendered layout.tsx.

Step 1: Create the Client Wrapper
```TypeScript
// components/ThemeProvider.tsx
"use client"; 

import { createContext } from 'react';

export const ThemeContext = createContext({});

export default function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <ThemeContext.Provider value={{ theme: 'dark' }}>
      {children}
    </ThemeContext.Provider>
  );
}
```
Step 2: Import into Server Layout
Do NOT add "use client" to layout.tsx. Keep it as a Server Component for SEO. Passing {children} inside the client provider allows nested routes to remain server-rendered.

```TypeScript
// app/layout.tsx
import ThemeProvider from '@/components/ThemeProvider';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <ThemeProvider>
          {children}
        </ThemeProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```
